note: Banks in the Northern Mariana Islands are numbered within the United States' routing number system: the American Bankers Association's Routing Number Policy and Procedures (the Routing Number Administrative Board's policy, revised 9/20, read 2026-10-30 on aba.com) defines a Federal Reserve District as one of the twelve areas assigned to a Federal Reserve Bank main office and says all of the United States and its territories fall into one of these twelve districts, whose routing symbols (01-12) begin a bank's routing number; and the FDIC's BankFind data (read 2026-10-30) lists 7 FDIC-insured bank offices in the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, at Saipan, Rota and Tinian (Bank of Guam, Bank of Hawaii, the Bank of the Federated States of Micronesia, BankPacific and First Hawaiian Bank). So an account there is numbered as one in the United States: a routing number and an account number of one to seventeen characters. (Wave 8's file, held for want of the account's length, gave the routing number alone; the United States' own form now takes the account.) No bank's own routing number page was read for the islands.

sources.title: American Bankers Association, Routing Number Policy and Procedures (revised 9/20)
sources.said: Federal Reserve District One of the twelve geographic areas assigned to a Federal Reserve Bank main office. All of the United States and its territories fall into one of these twelve districts.
